paragraphs: R' Pazi. R' Yehudah ben Poy said in R' Pazi's name, chapter Eizehu Neshekh. It is not there, but in Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:3:5: R' Yehudah ben Pazi said in R' Pazi's name, in R' Yohanan's name. If so, this is a sage, and not R' Hiyya's daughter. Tosafot, Bava Batra 149a, write that R' Shimon ben Pazi is identified by his mother, implying that Pazi is a woman's name (see above, Mari bar Rahel and R' Yosi ben Pazi). In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 12:3:3, and Horayot 3:5:15: the members of R' Hoshaya's household and those of bar Pazi used to greet the nasi every day. R' Hoshaya's people used to enter first and leave first. Bar Pazi's people went and intermarried with the patriarchal family; they then wished to enter first. R' Ammi was consulted. He said: ‘You shall erect the Tabernacle according to its rule’—a board that merited to be placed on the north shall be placed on the north, etc.; that is, whoever customarily entered first should enter first. In Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 3:1:15, and Sotah 9:16:3: one of R' Pazi's people—the nasi wished to enter into a marriage connection with him, but he declined, saying that he was unworthy to intermarry with the nasi's family. Before his death he ordered: ‘Clear the courtyard because of impurity, and prepare a chair for Yehoshafat king of Judah.’ He said [both Yerushalmi witnesses read “They said”]: ‘Let this man who pursued honor come after the man who fled honor.’ Hullin 46a: Ulla was before ben Pazi, and the patriarchal household sent to him. R' Aivu, ben Pazi, R' Yudan, and R' Yohanan (see there).
